d-pr-competitors.benediction: Go and compete today with open hands, blessing the very ones you are running against.

d-pr-through.title: On Praying Through a Decision
d-pr-through.situation: When you’ve asked God to bless a choice you’ve already made.
d-pr-through.verse: One of those days Jesus went out to a mountainside to pray, and spent the night praying to God. When morning came, he called his disciples to him and chose twelve of them, whom he also designated apostles.
d-pr-through.prayer: Father, here is the decision, still open, and here is my heart, not neutral. I confess the outcome I secretly want and the outcome I fear. Rearrange my desires until they can be trusted, and thin the fog enough for a next step. And whether or not you show me the answer, keep me company in the choosing.
d-pr-through.benediction: Decide nothing alone today — carry the open question up the mountainside first.

d-pr-short.title: On Prayers Between Meetings
d-pr-short.situation: When there’s no time for anything longer than a breath.
d-pr-short.verse: The king said to me, ‘What is it you want?’ Then I prayed to the God of heaven, and I answered the king.
d-pr-short.prayer: God of heaven, thank you that you hear the prayers I manage between meetings — the stairwell sentences, the one-word pleas. Teach me to aim those breaths at you all day long. Let the short prayers keep me honest and the long ones keep me rooted. And when the stakes are highest and the time is shortest, pray in me what I cannot compose.
d-pr-short.benediction: Move through your crowded day breathing prayers upward, for the God of heaven hears every one.

d-sc-feed.title: On the Word Before the Feed
d-sc-feed.situation: When the phone gets the first minutes of your day.
d-sc-feed.verse: I rise before dawn and cry for help; I have put my hope in your word.
d-sc-feed.prayer: Father, you know how fast my hand goes to the phone and how slowly it goes to your Word. Speak first tomorrow morning; let your voice set the terms of my day. Teach me to put my hope where the psalmist put his. Meet me before the noise does.
d-sc-feed.benediction: Go into this day with God’s word as the first word, and let every other voice come second.

d-sc-slow.title: On Reading Slowly
d-sc-slow.situation: When you skim everything, even Scripture.
d-sc-slow.verse: …whose delight is in the law of the Lord, and who meditates on his law day and night. That person is like a tree planted by streams of water, which yields its fruit in season and whose leaf does not wither.
d-sc-slow.prayer: Lord, I confess I read your Word the way I read everything else — fast, and looking for the takeaway. Slow me down. Give me delight where I have only had discipline, and roots where I have only had speed. Plant me by the stream and keep me there.
d-sc-slow.benediction: Go slowly into a fast day, rooted like a tree by water that does not run dry.

d-sc-carry.title: On Carrying One Verse
d-sc-carry.situation: When the morning reading is forgotten by the first meeting.
d-sc-carry.verse: Keep this Book of the Law always on your lips; meditate on it day and night, so that you may be careful to do everything written in it. Then you will be prosperous and successful.
d-sc-carry.prayer: Father, I keep leaving your Word behind with the breakfast dishes. Give me one verse today and keep it on my lips. Bring it back to me in the moments when I most need to remember who you are. Walk with me through the workday, not just the quiet one.
d-sc-carry.benediction: Go with the Word on your lips, and let it speak in the rooms where your day is decided.

d-sc-dry.title: On Dry Seasons in the Word
d-sc-dry.situation: When the Bible feels flat and you feel nothing.
d-sc-dry.verse: As the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return to it without watering the earth and making it bud and flourish … so is my word that goes out from my mouth: It will not return to me empty, but will accomplish what I desire and achieve the purpose for which I sent it.
d-sc-dry.prayer: Lord, your Word feels dry to me right now, and I confess I am tempted to quit. Thank you that your rain does its work whether or not I feel it fall. Keep me in the field; keep the Book open in front of me. Bring the green shoots in your own time.
d-sc-dry.benediction: Go on through the dry season, and trust the rain that never returns empty.

d-sc-small.title: On Starting Small and Staying
d-sc-small.situation: When every reading plan you start collapses in a busy week.
d-sc-small.verse: Jesus answered, ‘It is written: “Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.”’
d-sc-small.prayer: Father, forgive my heroic plans and my quiet quitting, and teach me the humility of bread. Give me a portion of your Word small enough to keep and rich enough to live on. When I miss a day, bring me back without shame. Feed me daily, as you promised.
d-sc-small.benediction: Go and eat your daily bread — small, steady, and enough for today.

d-gv-model.title: On Building Giving In
d-gv-model.situation: When generosity keeps waiting for a better quarter.
d-gv-model.verse: When you reap the harvest of your land, do not reap to the very edges of your field or gather the gleanings of your harvest. Do not go over your vineyard a second time or pick up the grapes that have fallen. Leave them for the poor and the foreigner. I am the Lord your God.
d-gv-model.prayer: Father, every field I work was yours before I ever touched it. Forgive me for treating generosity as a bonus feature instead of a load-bearing wall. Help me design giving into the structure of this business, where no bad quarter can quietly delete it. Make my company a field with edges left unreaped.
d-gv-model.benediction: Go and build the edges of your field for someone who will never see your spreadsheet.

d-gv-credit.title: On Giving Away the Credit
d-gv-credit.situation: When you did the work and want the world to know.
d-gv-credit.verse: He must become greater; I must become less.
d-gv-credit.prayer: Lord, you know how tightly I hold recognition, and how much of my hunger for credit is really hunger for assurance. Settle me in your verdict over my life, so applause becomes something I can pass along instead of collect. Show me one person this week whose work deserves the light I have been standing in. Make me glad, not grudging, when their name is spoken instead of mine.
d-gv-credit.benediction: Go and spend your spotlight on someone who has never stood in one.

d-gv-thin.title: On Giving from Thin Margins
d-gv-thin.situation: When there is barely enough for the business, let alone for others.
d-gv-thin.verse: In the midst of a very severe trial, their overflowing joy and their extreme poverty welled up in rich generosity. For I testify that they gave as much as they were able, and even beyond their ability.
d-gv-thin.prayer: Father, you see the numbers that keep me up at night, and you see how scarcity is teaching my hands to close. I confess I have made giving conditional on comfort. Loosen my grip, even a little, in this lean season. Let one small act of generosity declare that you, not my revenue, are holding me up.
d-gv-thin.benediction: Go and let a small gift in a lean season say what a large one never could.

d-gv-knowledge.title: On Open-Handed Knowledge
d-gv-knowledge.situation: When what you know feels like your only moat.
d-gv-knowledge.prayer: Lord, thank you for every person who taught me for nothing, and forgive me for pricing what I was handed as a gift. Free me from the fear that sharing what I know will shrink what I have. Give me eyes for one hungry learner — even a competitor’s — whom I can help this month. Make my knowledge a river, not a reservoir.
d-gv-knowledge.benediction: Go and teach someone the thing that cost you the most to learn.

d-gv-quiet.title: On the Quiet Gift
d-gv-quiet.situation: When no one would ever know if you gave — or if you didn’t.
d-gv-quiet.verse: But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing, so that your giving may be in secret. Then your Father, who sees what is done in secret, will reward you.
d-gv-quiet.prayer: Father, so much of my life is performed that I hardly know how to do a thing quietly anymore. Teach me the freedom of the gift that earns no post, no thanks, no strategic goodwill. Give me one secret generosity to carry, and the strength to keep it secret. It is enough that you see.
d-gv-quiet.benediction: Go and hide one act of generosity where only your Father will find it.

d-in-fudge.title: On the Numbers That Round Up
d-in-fudge.situation: When the metrics are almost true.
d-in-fudge.verse: Honest scales and balances belong to the Lord; all the weights in the bag are of his making.
d-in-fudge.prayer: Lord, you own the scales I weigh my company on. Forgive me for the roundings that flatter me and mislead others. Give me the courage to report what is, not what I wish were true. Teach me to trust you with the smaller, truer number.
d-in-fudge.benediction: Go and weigh honestly — the God who owns the scales can be trusted with the total.

d-in-costly.title: On Truth That Costs the Deal
d-in-costly.situation: When honesty might lose you the customer.
d-in-costly.verse: Truthful lips endure forever, but a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
d-in-costly.prayer: Father, I confess how much I want the deal, and how flexible the truth becomes when I want something. Steady me before the moment comes. Let me answer honestly even while I watch the revenue walk out the door. I trust you to build this company without my embellishment.
d-in-costly.benediction: Go and speak plainly — what is built on truthful lips endures.

d-in-gray.title: On What Everyone Else Does
d-in-gray.situation: When the whole industry calls it normal.
d-in-gray.verse: Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind. Then you will be able to test and approve what God’s will is — his good, pleasing and perfect will.
d-in-gray.prayer: Lord, I have inherited habits from my industry without ever testing them. Renew my mind until I can see the water I swim in. Show me the accepted practice you are asking me to leave behind. Give me the quiet nerve to be different without being self-righteous.
d-in-gray.benediction: Go unconformed — let the renewed mind, not the industry, set the pattern.

d-in-word.title: On Keeping Your Word
d-in-word.situation: When the promise costs more than it did.
d-in-word.verse: When you make a vow to God, do not delay to fulfill it. He has no pleasure in fools; fulfill your vow. It is better not to make a vow than to make one and not fulfill it.
d-in-word.prayer: Father, you are the God who keeps covenant at your own expense. I want to be like you in my small dealings. Strengthen me to keep the promise that has grown expensive, and humble me to go openly to anyone whose promise I cannot keep. Make my word a place where people can rest.
d-in-word.benediction: Go and fulfill what your lips have promised — you serve a God who kept his word at a cross.

d-in-unseen.title: On the Unwatched Hours
d-in-unseen.situation: When no one on the team is watching.
d-in-unseen.verse: Search me, God, and know my heart; test me and know my anxious thoughts. See if there is any offensive way in me, and lead me in the way everlasting.
d-in-unseen.prayer: God, you already see the rooms no one on my team enters. Search me there — I open the door instead of guarding it. Show me the private habit that does not match my public self. Form me in the unwatched hours until I am one person everywhere.
d-in-unseen.benediction: Go fully seen and fully loved — and let the unwatched hours make you whole.

d-wt-hidden.title: On the Hidden Season
d-wt-hidden.situation: When weeks go by and nothing visible is happening.
d-wt-hidden.verse: This is what the kingdom of God is like. A man scatters seed on the ground. Night and day, whether he sleeps or gets up, the seed sprouts and grows, though he does not know how.
d-wt-hidden.prayer: Father, I confess I equate your activity with visible progress. Teach me the patience of the farmer who sleeps because he trusts the seed. Work in the hidden places of this company, and in the hidden places of me. Help me believe you are moving when I can see nothing.
d-wt-hidden.benediction: Go and rest tonight like the farmer, trusting the God who grows seed in the dark.

d-wt-outofhands.title: On What Is Out of Your Hands
d-wt-outofhands.situation: When the term sheet, the signature, or the yes is out of your hands.
d-wt-outofhands.verse: In the Lord’s hand the king’s heart is a stream of water that he channels toward all who please him.
d-wt-outofhands.prayer: Lord, this decision is out of my hands, and I keep pretending otherwise. I place the investor, the signature, the answer into your hands, where they already were. Give me peace while I wait, and grace to trust you with either answer. Keep my heart soft toward the people I’m waiting on.
d-wt-outofhands.benediction: Go into this day with open hands, trusting the One who channels rivers and hearts.

d-wt-planting.title: On Planting for Distant Harvests
d-wt-planting.situation: When today’s work won’t pay off for years.
d-wt-planting.verse: Thus the saying ‘One sows and another reaps’ is true. I sent you to reap what you have not worked for. Others have done the hard work, and you have reaped the benefits of their labor.
d-wt-planting.prayer: God of the harvest, forgive my hurry to reap everything I sow. Give me the faith to plant what I may never see mature. Make me generous with work whose reward belongs to someone else. I trust you with the reaping.
d-wt-planting.benediction: Plant today what another generation may harvest, and be glad.

d-wt-forcing.title: On Forcing Doors
d-wt-forcing.situation: When you’re tempted to force open a door God hasn’t opened.
d-wt-forcing.verse: In repentance and rest is your salvation, in quietness and trust is your strength, but you would have none of it.
d-wt-forcing.prayer: Father, you know which door I’ve been trying to force. I am tired of pushing, and afraid of what waiting might cost me. Give me the quietness and trust you promise are my strength. Keep me from any yes I would have to manufacture myself.
d-wt-forcing.benediction: Wait at the door in quietness and trust, and let God be the one to open it.

d-wt-formed.title: On What Waiting Makes of You
d-wt-formed.situation: When the delay feels like wasted time.
d-wt-formed.verse: Let perseverance finish its work so that you may be mature and complete, not lacking anything.
d-wt-formed.prayer: Lord, I have treated this waiting season as an enemy. Thank you that you are forming something in me that arriving never could. Let perseverance finish its work, even when I want to rush it. Make me the kind of person who can carry what I’m asking for.
d-wt-formed.benediction: Stay in the waiting with hope, and let perseverance finish its good work in you.

d-cr-ask.title: On the Ask You Keep Postponing
d-cr-ask.situation: When the call, the raise, or the price increase keeps sliding to tomorrow.
d-cr-ask.verse: For if you remain silent at this time, relief and deliverance for the Jews will arise from another place … And who knows but that you have come to your royal position for such a time as this?
d-cr-ask.prayer: Father, you know the ask I keep postponing, and you know the fear underneath it. Thank you that your purposes do not hang on my performance, and that in Christ I already have the yes that matters most. Give me the courage to stop circling and to say the words plainly. Whatever the answer, keep my heart quiet in you.
d-cr-ask.benediction: Go and ask plainly, for the answer that defines you has already been given in Christ.

d-cr-obedience.title: On Courage as Obedience
d-cr-obedience.situation: When you are waiting to feel brave before you act.
d-cr-obedience.verse: ‘Be strong, all you people of the land,’ declares the Lord, ‘and work. For I am with you,’ declares the Lord Almighty.
d-cr-obedience.prayer: Lord, I confess I have been waiting to feel brave, and the feeling has not come. Teach me that your presence, not my confidence, is the ground I stand on. Show me the next act of plain obedience in front of me today. Make me strong enough to simply do it, whether or not my heart races.
d-cr-obedience.benediction: Go and do the assigned work, for the Lord Almighty is with you in it.

d-cr-reputation.title: On Risking Your Name
d-cr-reputation.situation: When doing the right thing could cost you your reputation.
d-cr-reputation.verse: If we are thrown into the blazing furnace, the God we serve is able to deliver us from it … But even if he does not, we want you to know, Your Majesty, that we will not serve your gods or worship the image of gold you have set up.
d-cr-reputation.prayer: Father, you know how carefully I have built my name, and how afraid I am to spend it. Settle in me the conviction that your verdict outweighs every room I will ever stand in. Give me the courage to tell the truth and do what is right, even without a guarantee of rescue. Hide my reputation with Christ, where no loss can reach it.
d-cr-reputation.benediction: Go and tell the truth, even if he does not deliver you the way you hoped, for your name is safe with him.

d-cr-reckless.title: On Faith and Recklessness
d-cr-reckless.situation: When you can’t tell if the leap is faith or foolishness.
d-cr-reckless.verse: But we prayed to our God and posted a guard day and night to meet this threat.
d-cr-reckless.prayer: Lord, help me tell the difference between the risk you are asking of me and the gamble my restlessness wants. Keep me from calling impatience faith, and from calling unbelief prudence. Give me the humility to count the cost and seek counsel, and the courage to move when you say move. Let both my praying and my planning honor you.
d-cr-reckless.benediction: Go and take the risks obedience requires — praying like Nehemiah, and posting the guard.

d-cr-first.title: On Going First
d-cr-first.situation: When your team is watching to see if you’ll take the first step.
d-cr-first.verse: Jonathan said to his young armor-bearer, ‘Come, let’s go over to the outpost … Perhaps the Lord will act in our behalf. Nothing can hinder the Lord from saving, whether by many or by few.’
d-cr-first.prayer: Father, forgive me for the times I have pointed at risks instead of taking them. Thank you that Jesus went first through the hardest ground, so that I follow a cleared path. Give me Jonathan’s humble confidence — no guarantees, but full trust that nothing can hinder you. Make my courage something my team can borrow.
d-cr-first.benediction: Go first up the rocks, and let those who follow find the path already walked.

d-hu-junior.title: On Listening Down
d-hu-junior.situation: When the best idea in the room comes from the newest hire.
d-hu-junior.verse: Listen to advice and accept discipline, and at the end you will be counted among the wise.
d-hu-junior.prayer: Father, I confess that I weigh advice by the rank of the person giving it. Forgive my deafness to the voices you have placed below me on a chart you never drew. Settle my identity so deeply in Christ that a better idea feels like a gift and not a threat. Give me ears today for wisdom, wherever you send it from.
d-hu-junior.benediction: Go into your day with open ears, and let wisdom find you through whomever God chooses.

d-hu-wrong.title: On Saying It Out Loud
d-hu-wrong.situation: When you were wrong and the whole team watched it happen.
d-hu-wrong.verse: Whoever conceals their sins does not prosper, but the one who confesses and renounces them finds mercy.
d-hu-wrong.prayer: Lord, you know the call I got wrong and the ways I have been polishing the story since. I do not want to manage this; I want to confess it. Thank you that in Christ my standing does not depend on a spotless record. Give me the courage to say plainly to my team what I am saying now to you.
d-hu-wrong.benediction: Walk out of hiding today, and let mercy do what image management never could.

d-hu-selfmade.title: On the Self-Made Myth
d-hu-selfmade.situation: When “I built this myself” starts to feel true.
d-hu-selfmade.verse: For who makes you different from anyone else? What do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you did not?
d-hu-selfmade.prayer: Father, forgive me for taking credit for the materials. I did the work, but you gave the mind, the moment, the people, and the strength — and I have called the sum of your gifts my achievement. Teach me to receive: help, counsel, grace, all of it. Make me a grateful builder instead of a self-made one.
d-hu-selfmade.benediction: Go and build with open hands, remembering the Giver in everything you are tempted to call your own.

d-hu-praise.title: On Being Tested by Praise
d-hu-praise.situation: When the press is good and everyone is clapping.
d-hu-praise.verse: The crucible for silver and the furnace for gold, but people are tested by their praise.
d-hu-praise.prayer: Lord, thank you for the encouragement of this season — I receive it as kindness from your hand. But keep my ear tuned to your voice above the crowd’s, because crowds turn and you do not. Let praise pass through me as gratitude rather than settle in me as need. Keep me the same person in public that I am before you in secret.
d-hu-praise.benediction: Carry the applause lightly, and let your Father’s voice remain the loudest one you hear.

d-hu-freedom.title: On Not Being the Smartest
d-hu-freedom.situation: When you feel you have to have every answer in the room.
d-hu-freedom.verse: Humble yourselves, therefore, under God’s mighty hand, that he may lift you up in due time. Cast all your anxiety on him because he cares for you.
d-hu-freedom.prayer: Father, I am tired of performing omniscience. I humble myself under your mighty hand and hand you the anxiety that came bundled with my pride. Thank you that you know my limits fully and love me anyway. Free me to ask, to listen, and to be gladly outthought by the people you have given me.
d-hu-freedom.benediction: Go in the freedom of the lifted burden, and let God be the one who raises you up.

d-fo-replay.title: On the Argument You Keep Replaying
d-fo-replay.situation: When you still rehearse the fight with someone who wronged you.
d-fo-replay.verse: Bear with each other and forgive one another if any of you has a grievance against someone. Forgive as the Lord forgave you.
d-fo-replay.prayer: Lord, you know the argument I keep winning in my head and losing in my heart. I hand you the grievance, the unsaid speech, the verdict I keep demanding. Forgive them through me, the way you forgave me before I ever apologized. Quiet the replay and give the room back to peace.
d-fo-replay.benediction: Go and leave the courtroom in your head unattended — the Judge you trust is already seated.

d-fo-boundaries.title: On Forgiving With Your Eyes Open
d-fo-boundaries.situation: When you can release the debt but shouldn’t re-sign the contract.
d-fo-boundaries.verse: Above all else, guard your heart, for everything you do flows from it.
d-fo-boundaries.prayer: Father, teach me the difference between a grudge and a guardrail. I release this person from the debt I have been carrying against them. Give me the honesty to remember what happened and the mercy to want their good anyway. Guard my heart without hardening it.
d-fo-boundaries.benediction: Go and be both merciful and wise — cancel the debt, and keep the fence in good repair.

d-fo-unapologized.title: On the Apology That Never Came
d-fo-unapologized.situation: When the person who hurt the business has never said sorry.
d-fo-unapologized.verse: Jesus said, ‘Father, forgive them, for they do not know what they are doing.’ And they divided up his clothes by casting lots.
d-fo-unapologized.prayer: Father, I have been waiting for an apology to unlock my forgiveness, and the waiting has become its own prison. I bring you the wound while it is still unacknowledged. Forgive them — and loosen my grip on the words they never said. Settle my account with you, since it cannot be settled with them.
d-fo-unapologized.benediction: Go and be free of the sorry that never came — the Father heard your case, and it is settled.

d-fo-self.title: On Forgiving the Founder in the Mirror
d-fo-self.situation: When your own decision is the one you can’t forgive.
d-fo-self.verse: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.
d-fo-self.prayer: Lord, you know the decision I cannot stop retrying, and the people it cost. I confess what was truly mine to confess, and I receive what you have already declared: no condemnation. Teach me to grieve the harm without wearing the sentence. Make me careful and free at the same time.
d-fo-self.benediction: Go out from the courtroom of one — the Judge has ruled, and his ruling is mercy.

d-fo-rival.title: On Closing the Mental Courtroom
d-fo-rival.situation: When a rival lives rent-free in the docket of your mind.
d-fo-rival.verse: Do not take revenge, my dear friends, but leave room for God’s wrath, for it is written: ‘It is mine to avenge; I will repay,’ says the Lord.
d-fo-rival.prayer: Lord, I hand you the case I have been building against my rival — the charges, the evidence, the sentence I drafted. It was never mine to try. Free the hours and the energy that resentment has been spending for me. Let me build with clean hands and an undivided mind.
d-fo-rival.benediction: Go and build instead of prosecute — the bench is occupied, and the Judge is just.

d-vo-ministry.title: On Business as Ministry
d-vo-ministry.situation: When your work feels like a lesser calling than the pulpit.
d-vo-ministry.verse: And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.
d-vo-ministry.prayer: Father, forgive me for treating my work as second-class in your kingdom. Thank you that Jesus sanctified ordinary labor with his own hands. Teach me to do everything this week in his name, with gratitude. Make my company a place where your goodness is tasted, not just talked about.
d-vo-ministry.benediction: Go and do your whole day’s work in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks as you go.

d-vo-drift.title: On Drifted Vision
d-vo-drift.situation: When the company no longer looks like the dream and you wonder if you missed your calling.
d-vo-drift.verse: Many are the plans in a person’s heart, but it is the Lord’s purpose that prevails.
d-vo-drift.prayer: Lord, I confess I have mourned the company I imagined and resented the one you gave me. Thank you that your purpose does not depend on my plans surviving. Show me what you are actually building here, and give me eyes to love it. I trust that I am not lost to you.
d-vo-drift.benediction: Walk into the company you actually have, trusting that the Lord’s purpose is prevailing there.

d-vo-ambition.title: On Surrendered Ambition
d-vo-ambition.situation: When you wonder whether wanting to build something great is a sin to kill or a fire to steward.
d-vo-ambition.verse: Take delight in the Lord, and he will give you the desires of your heart.
d-vo-ambition.prayer: Father, I do not know how to hold ambition without being held by it. I hand you my dreams for this company — keep what you planted and burn what I invented. Teach me to delight in you before I delight in progress. Be the joy underneath my drive.
d-vo-ambition.benediction: Carry your ambition with open hands, and let the Lord himself be your delight.

d-vo-city.title: On Building for the City
d-vo-city.situation: When the exit has become the whole point and you’ve forgotten who the business is for.
d-vo-city.verse: Also, seek the peace and prosperity of the city to which I have carried you into exile. Pray to the Lord for it, because if it prospers, you too will prosper.
d-vo-city.prayer: Lord, you placed this company in a real city full of people you love. Forgive me for building with one eye on the door. Show me how our work can seek this place’s peace and prosperity, and teach me to pray for it by name. Bind our good to our neighbors’ good.
d-vo-city.benediction: Go and seek the peace of the city where God has planted you, and find your own peace inside it.

d-vo-serve.title: On Who You Serve
d-vo-serve.situation: When your identity has collapsed into your job title.
d-vo-serve.verse: Serve wholeheartedly, as if you were serving the Lord, not people, because you know that the Lord will reward each one of them for whatever good they do, whether they are slave or free.
d-vo-serve.prayer: Lord Jesus, I confess I have let my title tell me who I am. You are my true Master, and this company is an assignment from your hand. Teach me to serve you wholeheartedly inside the work, and to hold the work itself loosely. Keep my name safe with you.
d-vo-serve.benediction: Go and serve wholeheartedly, knowing that the Master you work for never forgets what is done for him.

d-en-yearfive.title: On Year Five
d-en-yearfive.situation: When the novelty is long gone and the work remains.
d-en-yearfive.verse: You need to persevere so that when you have done the will of God, you will receive what he has promised.
d-en-yearfive.prayer: Father, the shine has worn off this work, and I confess I miss it. Thank you that your promises do not fade the way my feelings do. Give me perseverance for the unglamorous middle, and eyes to see you in it. Keep me faithful today, and let that be enough.
d-en-yearfive.benediction: Go and do the will of God one more ordinary day, trusting the promise that waits on the far side of perseverance.

d-en-race.title: On Running Your Own Race
d-en-race.situation: When others exit rich and you’re still building.
d-en-race.verse: Therefore, since we are surrounded by such a great cloud of witnesses, let us throw off everything that hinders and the sin that so easily entangles. And let us run with perseverance the race marked out for us, fixing our eyes on Jesus, the pioneer and perfecter of faith.
d-en-race.prayer: Lord, I confess the ache I feel when others finish rich while I am still climbing. Forgive my sideways glances and the quiet accounting of envy. Fix my eyes on Jesus, who endured for the joy set before him. Help me run the race you marked out for me, and no one else’s.
d-en-race.benediction: Run with perseverance the race marked out for you, eyes fixed on the One who has already finished it.

d-en-renewal.title: On Strength That Renews
d-en-renewal.situation: When your reserves are spent and the road is still long.
d-en-renewal.verse: But those who hope in the Lord will renew their strength. They will soar on wings like eagles; they will run and not grow weary, they will walk and not be faint.
d-en-renewal.prayer: God of unwearied strength, I have been running on my own reserves, and they are nearly gone. Teach me to hope in you rather than in my stamina. Renew my strength for this season, whether it calls for soaring, running, or simply walking without fainting. I wait on you today.
d-en-renewal.benediction: Walk on without fainting, drawing today’s strength from the God who never tires.

d-en-compound.title: On the Compounding of Small Days
d-en-compound.situation: When today’s faithfulness feels too small to matter.
d-en-compound.verse: Therefore, my dear brothers and sisters, stand firm. Let nothing move you. Always give yourselves fully to the work of the Lord, because you know that your labor in the Lord is not in vain.
d-en-compound.prayer: Father, I keep looking for the dramatic day, and you keep handing me small ones. Thank you that no labor done in you is ever in vain, whether I see its fruit or not. Help me give myself fully to today’s small work and then actually rest. I trust the harvest to you.
d-en-compound.benediction: Give yourself fully to today’s small work — in the Lord, none of it is in vain.

d-en-weary.title: On Not Growing Weary
d-en-weary.situation: When you keep doing good and the results keep lagging.
d-en-weary.verse: And as for you, brothers and sisters, never tire of doing what is good.
d-en-weary.prayer: Lord, I am tired of doing good without seeing the good it does. Guard me from the cynicism that treats integrity as a failed experiment. Remind me that you see every honest ledger and kept promise. Renew my resolve to do what is good, and leave the results with you.
d-en-weary.benediction: Go and do good one more day, unwearied, for the God who keeps the true accounts.
